prize_parts.citation: for developing targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, through PROTACs and the molecular-glue mechanism of thalidomide-class drugs

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation meets my own test of a game-changer: a new chemical principle (small molecules that recruit an E3 ligase to a chosen protein and trigger its destruction) that has already changed how medicinal chemists approach targets once called undruggable. The principle is simple and general, the ternary-complex mechanism is quantitatively understood and structurally confirmed, and cereblon recasts thalidomide-type drugs as molecular glues. Five of us put it in the top three in our openings, and that convergence came from members with different backgrounds. That counts for something even though support is not merit. The attribution is also tractable: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept, and Handa identified cereblon, the mechanistic anchor for glue degraders.
statement.case_against: Clinical validation is still incomplete, since few or no degraders are approved, and I rank maturity above hype. The three-person limit also forces a painful cut: Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure), Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim all have real claims, and Crews/Deshaies versus the glue discoverers is a genuine priority split between two distinct mechanisms. If the committee thinks a prize now would be early, B023 (energy landscape theory and folding experiment) is the better-matured choice, and I would not fight that outcome.

responses.point: Targeted degradation turns ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis into a designable chemical reaction and is a general chemical tool and therapeutic modality, so it should be first.
responses.response: I agree on the chemistry and have moved it above my own opening first choice, B023, because our broad convergence reflects a consequential mechanism and not just popularity. I part company on timing. You call the maturity sufficient while noting that no PROTAC is approved, and I think we should say plainly that the prize would honour a mechanism and modality, with the clinical payoff still developing. The citation should therefore name the principle, not the drug pipeline.

responses.point: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling by Buchwald and Hartwig is fully mature, used daily in medicinal and process chemistry, and its recognition is overdue.
responses.response: I find this the strongest competing case on maturity and on simplicity, which I value, and I kept B034 as an alternative. My reservation is the 2010 cross-coupling prize, which already covered adjacent Pd chemistry and may make this a less novel step. That is a judgment about novelty, not about quality. I also think we should decide whether Kosugi belongs, since clean Buchwald and Hartwig attribution is the strength of your case and a third name dilutes it.

responses.point: Long-range electron transfer in proteins (Gray and Winkler) put biological charge transport on a quantitative physical footing and is mature, with decades of independent confirmation.
responses.response: It is an excellent quantitative story and I respect the maturity, but I doubt it clears the game-changer bar for a prize now. Marcus theory was already honoured in 1992, and the tunnelling-pathway theory sits outside the credited pair, so the Gray and Winkler pairing leaves much of the conceptual credit elsewhere. I would need the committee to explain what the prize adds beyond what the 1992 recognition established. I would take your Shokat and KRAS case more seriously, since the attribution is clean, but it competes directly with B036 in the same medicinal chemistry space.

responses.point: Phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell is a physically grounded, original idea that reframed cell compartmentalization, and the core principle is mature enough.
responses.response: As Chair you rank it first, and I accept that it is original and well confirmed. My concern is that the in vivo interpretation of specific condensates is still debated, and that Pappu and Mittag's sequence-grammar contributions sit awkwardly outside a three-name cut. I would want evidence that the chemistry, and not only the cell biology, carries the prize before I put it ahead of degradation. I do not see that evidence yet, but I am open to it.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the absence of an approved PROTAC drug as too early for a prize.
Whether Handa (molecular-glue mechanism) or Ciulli (VHL ligands and ternary-complex structure) is the better third name beside Crews and Deshaies.
Whether energy landscape theory (B023) would be treated as chemistry rather than physics or biophysics, and whether it overlaps too much with the 2024 protein structure prize.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the proposed laureates. My Warshel/EVB and ribosome ties are unrelated to B036, and I know none of the credited persons personally.
